sections.name: File setup, AssistantSource, AssistantMessage, AssistantProposal
sections.title: Shared message and proposal shapes
sections.what: Defines the data shapes for chat messages, source links and proposed wording changes, so the parent screen and this panel agree on them.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the message and proposal data consistent across screens.
sections.watch_out: A message marked as recorded changes whether the no-cited-facts warning appears.

sections.name: LessonsAssistant (part 1)
sections.title: Panel setup and submit
sections.what: Sets up the panel: a header with a mode note, the draft question, and an automatic scroll to the newest message. When submitted, the question is trimmed and sent, and the draft is cleared only if the send succeeded.
sections.why: The header note says answers quote saved facts only, with no web research.
sections.watch_out: Because the draft is kept after a failure, a retry does not need retyping.

sections.name: LessonsAssistant (part 2)
sections.title: Message list and proposal card
sections.what: Shows a loading placeholder, then the message list. User questions appear in a dark bubble on the right and answers on the left. Each answer shows its sources, up to six fact buttons with a link to all sources, a revision number, and a warning when no facts are cited. A proposal card shows the before and after wording with Apply and Dismiss buttons while pending, or a status note afterwards.
sections.why: The warning for answers with no cited facts shows where support is missing.
sections.watch_out: Only six fact buttons are shown per answer, so the all-sources link is the only route to the rest.

sections.name: LessonsAssistant (part 3)
sections.title: Errors, suggestions and input box
sections.what: Shows any error with a reload button, a row of suggested questions, the question box (Enter sends, Shift plus Enter adds a new line), an Ask button, and a note explaining why asking is disabled when it is.
sections.why: Likely reason: Enter-to-send is a common chat pattern. Not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Questions are capped at 4000 characters. The disabled state blocks both the button and the Enter key.

summary: The question-and-answer panel in a lessons analysis. A reader asks about the saved run and sees answers linked to their evidence, plus proposed wording changes that can be accepted or dismissed.
purpose: Answer questions only from facts already recorded in the saved run.
why: The file header says the panel is read-only, quotes recorded facts only, and does no web research. In replay mode it is shown without sending requests.
how: 1. Keeps the draft question. 2. Scrolls to the newest message. 3. On submit, trims the question, sends it, and clears the box only if the send succeeded. 4. Shows messages, source buttons, fact buttons, a warning for answers with no cited facts, a proposed amendment card, and a loading line. 5. Shows errors, suggested questions and the input box.
inputs: Messages, a lookup of facts by ID, citation and fact-check callbacks, the ask callback, pending and error state, optional suggested questions, and an optional proposal.
outputs: The panel on screen. Asking calls the ask callback. Apply or dismiss calls the proposal's decision callback.
risks: A failed question stays in the box on purpose. Only six fact buttons show per answer, so the all-sources link is needed for the rest. An answer with no cited facts is flagged as unsupported.
debug: If an answer shows No facts cited, check the recorded facts behind that answer. If the Ask button stays off, read the disabled reason text under the box. If a proposal does not update, check its status and its decision callback.
